summary: Untrusted input reaching an interpreter, query, template, file path, parser, deserializer or outbound request without neutralization on the path, traced through source and SAST, CodeQL and CPG evidence.
looks_for: SQL, HQL/JPQL or ORM raw-query strings built by concatenation, format strings or template literals from request data
NoSQL queries that accept request objects as operators ($where, $ne, $regex) or build query documents from parsed JSON bodies
shell execution with shell=True, exec/system/popen, backticks or child_process.exec on strings containing input; argument arrays whose leading argument is input-controlled (option injection)
eval, Function, exec, dynamic import, reflection or expression-language evaluation (SpEL, OGNL, MVEL, JEXL) over input
server-side template rendering where input becomes the template source rather than a template variable (Jinja2, Freemarker, Velocity, Handlebars, Twig)
file paths joined from input without canonicalization and base-directory check: downloads, uploads, archive extraction (zip slip), include/require
XML parsers with external entities or DTDs enabled; YAML full loaders; native deserializers (pickle, Java ObjectInputStream, BinaryFormatter, PHP unserialize) on untrusted bytes
HTTP clients whose URL, host or port comes from input (webhooks, fetch-by-URL, proxies, redirects followed server-side): SSRF toward metadata or internal services
LDAP filters, XPath expressions and HTTP header values assembled from input without escaping
HTML, JavaScript or attribute contexts receiving input with auto-escaping disabled (|safe, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, v-html, innerHTML, raw)
sanitizers or validators that are applied on one route but not on a sibling route, version or content type reaching the same sink
CodeQL, Semgrep/Opengrep or Joern CPG flows whose source is a request, message or file input and whose sink is one of the above
preconditions: an attacker-reachable entry point (route, queue consumer, file import, CLI argument from an untrusted caller) supplies the tainted value
the value reaches the sink in a form that changes its structure: query or command syntax, template source, path segment, URL authority, parser input
no neutralization on that path: parameter binding, allow-list, type coercion to a non-string, context-aware encoding, safe parser configuration
the authentication or authorization in front of the entry point is either absent or satisfiable by the attacker's assumed role
for SSRF: the server's network position reaches something the attacker cannot reach directly (metadata service, internal API, localhost admin port)
proof_obligations: the source at file:line (handler parameter, body field, header, message field) and why it is attacker-controlled
the sink at file:line with the exact API call that interprets the value
the data-flow path between them, from a CodeQL/Semgrep/Joern trace or hand-traced call chain with each hop cited at file:line
the absence of neutralization on that path shown by the code on each hop, not inferred from a function name
the route or entry-point registration at file:line that exposes the source, with its auth middleware or the lack of it
for XXE or deserialization: the parser or deserializer construction at file:line showing the unsafe setting or type, and the library version from the lockfile when the default depends on it
for SSRF: the client call at file:line, the controllable URL component, and the absence of scheme, host allow-list and post-resolution private-address checks
false_positive_traps: parameterized queries misread as concatenation: placeholders (?, $1, :name, %s passed as a separate args tuple) with values bound by the driver
ORM query builders and criteria APIs that bind values even though the call site looks like string assembly
concatenated identifiers or fragments taken from a fixed allow-list, enum or constant map rather than from input
subprocess calls with an argument list and no shell where input cannot become an option or the executable
template engines with auto-escaping on, where the flagged value is a variable, not template source
SAST taint that starts from a trusted source (config file, environment, internal constant, admin-only migration script) or from test code
paths resolved and checked with realpath/canonical form against a base directory before use
URL fetches whose host is fixed by configuration and whose input only sets a path or query component on a trusted host
must_not: claim an injection from a sink alone; a finding needs a cited source-to-sink path
treat a SAST or CodeQL alert as proof without reading the flagged path in the source
send payloads to, or execute, the target; reason from source and tool evidence only
